subject: Post-call: budget anchor & commitment-tier exploration
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@cobaltai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 15:24:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: budget anchor & commitment-tier exploration

Hi Emma — thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying asks so we can put together a pricing draft that matches Cobalt's constraints.

Call summary (2 lines):
- You plan to embed Redwood for the new assistant product: intent classification + completion + embeddings for conversation retrieval.
- Target initial user base ~15k MAU scaled to 60k in 9–12 months with peak bursts.

Clarifying asks (so we tailor a commitment / discount proposal):
1) Monthly tokens (best-effort): do you expect ~tokens/month for production in month 1 vs month 6? A ballpark is fine (e.g., 100M -> 600M).
2) Target unit economics: is there an internal target $/1M tokens or monthly run-rate you want to hit? We often model to a $/1M number to show discount impact.
3) Budget range and procurement horizon (Q3 purchase? multi-year?).
4) Startup program eligibility: you mentioned pre-Series A — can you confirm legal entity and funding stage so we can check for the startup credit?

Next steps: if you can reply with the 4 items above by end of day Wednesday, we’ll send a 1-page pricing anchor + a 1-page committed-use scenario (3-, 6-, 12-month) and a highlighted SOW template for procurement to review.

Thanks — looking forward.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference — production-ready LLM inference

From: Emma Li <emma@cobaltai.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 09:17:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: budget anchor & commitment-tier exploration

Thanks Hannah — great recap. Answers below:

1) Monthly tokens (production steady-state assumptions):
- Month 1 (post-PoC roll): ~120M tokens
- Month 6: ~480M tokens (we expect usage ramp from ML-heavy experiments)

2) Target unit economics:
- We’d like to see scenarios around $750 — $1,200 per 1M tokens (USD) after discount; our procurement target is to get to <$900/1M if possible.

3) Budget & timing:
- We have a $90k budget for the initial 6 months of infra (not all for inference), procurement prefers Q3 commitments for volume pricing.
- Procurement lead timing: we can sign a 6–12 month committed use in Q3 if the economics line up.

4) Startup program eligibility:
- We’re pre-Series A (seed + small SAFEs), legal entity: Cobalt AI, Inc., incorporated in Delaware. If there’s an application or docs you need, let me know.

Other asks: can you show a committed-use example that includes a mid-year addendum (i.e., scale from 6 -> 12 months with a step-up band)? Also curious about any multi-year incentives if we commit to a 2-year ramp.

—Emma
Emma Li
Head of Product | Cobalt AI
emma@cobaltai.com
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 10:01:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Re: Post-call: budget anchor & commitment-tier exploration

Ben / Priyom — forwarding Emma’s reply from Cobalt. Key data points: 120M -> 480M tokens, budget signal $90k for first 6 months (infra + inference), procurement open to 6–12 month CPCs in Q3, wants <$900/1M ideally. They asked explicitly for:
- a committed-use example with a mid-year addendum (scale band),
- multi-year incentive examples (2-year ramp).

Notes / suggested approach:
- We should prepare: 1) a conservative 6-month commitment with starter discount that hits ~$950/1M, 2) an escalator path to 12 months showing blended $/1M at their expected growth, 3) a 2-year incentive table (rebates at milestones) to show upside.
- Include startup credit (if they qualify) as a one-time credit applied to month 1–2 usage vs. a straight % off. That preserves unit economics without over-discounting committed units.

Ben — can you draft the pricing anchor PDF with 3 scenarios (monthlies + blended $/1M + impact of a $10k startup credit)? Priyom — flag any technical risks for burst capacity or KV cache needs that change effective tokens (we should note delta between input tokens and billable tokens if we apply prefix caching).

I’ll follow up to Emma with the draft by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Hannah

Subject: Pricing anchor and next steps (attached)

Hi Emma — appreciate the quick turnaround. Attaching a 1-page pricing anchor and a 1-page committed-use scenario (redwood-pricing-draft-20270601.pdf) plus our standard SOW template for procurement. Highlights:

1) Scenarios (summary):
- Starter (no commit): list $1,450 / 1M tokens
- 6-month commit (baseline): $980 / 1M tokens (assumes 360M total over 6 months)
- 12-month stepped commit: blended $890 / 1M tokens with mid-year scale band (120M months 1–2, grow to 480M by month 6)

2) Startup credit: we can apply a one-time $10k credit (requires verification docs) — moves the effective first-2-month blended $/1M closer to $820 in the 6-month example.

3) Multi-year incentive: 2-year path offered as a rebate structure tied to annual committed volumes (5% rebate at year-end if annual commit exceeds threshold). We call this out as a separate addendum so procurement can evaluate.

4) Technical note: Priyom added a short note about prefix caching assumptions and burst headroom — large bursts can push billable tokens higher; recommend a small buffer in committed bands for cache misses.

Next steps:
- If procurement confirms eligibility for the startup credit, please send the verification doc and we’ll bake it into the quote.
- If the 12-month stepped commit is appealing, we can draft a short addendum that includes the mid-year scale band and the 2-year rebate schedule.
- I’ve shared the HubSpot deal record: https://hubspot.com/deal/DEAL-3482 and a Drive folder with the draft docs for procurement review.

Can you confirm whether procurement prefers a single PO now (6-month) or a conditional PO with a 12-month addendum? Once I have that we’ll hand to revenue ops for an official quote.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
